next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Upcoming Election

glance_notes.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — November 2026 Registration Deadline
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: North Carolina's regular voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is 5:00 p.m. on October 9. Eligible residents who miss that deadline may register and vote at the same time during the in-person early-voting period.

glance_notes.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Vote Early in Person
glance_notes.text: Early Voting & Same-Day Registration: In-person early voting for the November 3, 2026 General Election runs from October 15 through 3:00 p.m. October 31. Eligible residents may use same-day registration at early-voting sites during this period.

glance_notes.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Voter ID
glance_notes.text: Photo ID Required, With Exceptions: North Carolina voters are asked to show an acceptable photo ID when voting. A voter who cannot show acceptable photo identification may still vote by completing an ID Exception Form when a qualifying exception applies.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible North Carolina residents may register using a voter registration application submitted to their county board of elections. Existing North Carolina Division of Motor Vehicles customers with a North Carolina driver's license or identification card may also use the state's online DMV voter registration service. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, live in the North Carolina county where the person is registering, have resided there for at least 30 days before Election Day and be at least 18 years old by the date of the General Election. Eligible 16- and 17-year-olds may preregister. A person serving a felony sentence, including probation, parole or post-release supervision, is not eligible to register or vote until completing the felony sentence. Eligible residents who miss the regular registration deadline may register and immediately vote at an early-voting site during the same-day registration period.
register.glance_value: Mail, DMV online service and early-voting same-day registration
register.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Registering
register.internal_note: North Carolina's online voter registration is through NCDMV and is available to existing DMV customers with a North Carolina driver's license or DMV-issued ID. Do not characterize North Carolina as having unrestricted Election Day registration. General same-day registration is available during in-person early voting, not on Election Day. Special Election Day registration provisions exist for certain military voters. Felony eligibility should be stated carefully: voting rights are restored automatically upon completion of the felony sentence, including probation, parole or post-release supervision.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the North Carolina State Board of Elections Voter Search to check your registration status and voter record. The system also provides voter-specific information including Election Day polling places, voting districts and sample ballots after they are finalized.
check_registration.glance_value: Check through the official Voter Search
check_registration.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Voter Search
check_registration.internal_note: NCSBE repeatedly directs voters to Voter Search for registration status, polling places and finalized sample ballots. County boards of elections are the appropriate contact if a voter believes the record is incorrect.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: North Carolina's regular civilian voter registration deadline is 25 days before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline is 5:00 p.m. Friday, October 9. A mailed application is timely if postmarked on or before the deadline. Eligible residents who miss the regular deadline may register and vote at the same time at an in-person early-voting site in their county from October 15 through October 31. General same-day registration is not available on Election Day.
deadlines.glance_value: October 9; same-day registration during early voting
deadlines.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Voter Registration Deadlines
deadlines.internal_note: NCSBE directly establishes the October 9, 2026 deadline and the 25-day rule. Mail applications with a missing or unclear postmark can be processed for the election if received by the 20th day before Election Day. Same-day registration is available during early voting. There are special rules for military and overseas voters, including a narrow Election Day registration provision for certain uniformed-service voters who were absent when registration closed.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use North Carolina's official Voter Search or Election Day Polling Place Search to find your assigned Election Day polling place. On Election Day, registered voters generally must vote at their assigned polling place. During early voting, a voter may instead use any early-voting site in the voter's county. Because polling locations can change, voters should verify their location before Election Day.
polling_place.glance_value: Use Voter Search for your assigned Election Day site
polling_place.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Vote in Person on Election Day
polling_place.internal_note: NCSBE explicitly distinguishes Election Day voting at the assigned polling place from early voting, when voters may use any early-voting site in their county. This distinction is important and should remain in reader-facing guidance.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: North Carolina's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 6:30 a.m. until 7:30 p.m. A voter who is in line at the assigned polling place at 7:30 p.m. must be allowed to vote. North Carolina voters are asked to show an acceptable photo ID when checking in. A voter who cannot show acceptable photo identification may still be able to vote by completing an ID Exception Form. General same-day voter registration is not available on Election Day.
election_day.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — 2026 General Election Day
election_day.internal_note: NCSBE directly confirms November 3, 2026, 6:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m. hours and the right of voters already in line at closing to vote. Photo ID is currently required, but NCSBE emphasizes that all voters will be allowed to vote with or without photo ID because qualifying voters may use the ID Exception Form. Special Election Day registration rules for certain military voters are not the same as general same-day registration.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: North Carolina polling places are open from 6:30 a.m. until 7:30 p.m. on Election Day. Anyone who is in line to vote when the polls close must be permitted to vote. If a polling place experiences a qualifying delay or interruption, the State Board may authorize an extension of the closing time.
polling_hours.internal_note: G.S. 163-166.25 directly establishes 6:30 a.m.-7:30 p.m., protects voters already in line and authorizes the State Board to extend closing by an equivalent period when opening is delayed or voting is interrupted for more than 15 minutes.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: North Carolina provides in-person early voting before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting begins Thursday, October 15 and ends at 3:00 p.m. Saturday, October 31. Registered voters may vote at any early-voting site in their county. Eligible residents who are not registered in the county may also register and immediately vote at an early-voting site using same-day registration. Same-day registrants must provide proof of residence. Exact locations and operating hours vary by county.
early_voting.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Vote Early in Person
early_voting.internal_note: NCSBE directly confirms October 15 through 3:00 p.m. October 31 for the 2026 General Election. Same-day registration is available throughout this period. Voters registering through same-day registration must have lived in the county for at least 30 days before Election Day and must provide qualifying proof of residence.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Any registered North Carolina voter may request and vote an absentee-by-mail ballot without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the ordinary absentee-ballot request deadline is 5:00 p.m. Tuesday, October 20. Completed civilian absentee ballots must be received by the county board of elections by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day; an Election Day postmark by itself is not sufficient. Most absentee voters must have two witnesses or a notary observe the voter marking the ballot and must include a photocopy of acceptable photo identification in the designated envelope sleeve or complete an ID Exception Form. Military and overseas voters and qualifying blind or visually impaired voters have separate procedures.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse; request by 5:00 p.m. October 20
absentee_mail.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Vote By Mail
absentee_mail.internal_note: This section reflects a critical current North Carolina rule: civilian absentee ballots must be physically received by 7:30 p.m. Election Day. Older information describing a three-day post-election grace period is outdated. NCSBE's 2026 guidance also confirms the two-witness-or-notary requirement and photo-ID-copy/ID-Exception requirement. Absentee requests cannot be faxed or emailed; voters may use the online portal or submit the official paper form in person or by authorized delivery methods.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: North Carolina voters are asked to show acceptable photo identification when voting in person. Common acceptable IDs include a North Carolina driver's license, North Carolina identification card, U.S. passport or passport card, qualifying tribal identification and approved student or public-employee identification cards. Most accepted IDs must be unexpired or expired for one year or less, although state law provides additional rules for certain IDs and voters age 65 or older. A voter who cannot show an acceptable photo ID may still vote by completing an ID Exception Form when a qualifying exception applies. County boards of elections can issue free voter photo ID cards to registered voters.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID required; exception process and free ID available
voter_id.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Voter ID
voter_id.internal_note: Current NCSBE guidance says voters will be asked to show photo ID but also explicitly states that all voters will be allowed to vote with or without a photo ID because an ID Exception Form is available for qualifying circumstances. County boards issue free voter photo IDs with no supporting documents required, although a person cannot newly register in a county and receive that county voter ID card simultaneously because registration must first complete the address-verification process. Approved student and public-employee IDs listed by NCSBE are valid through December 31, 2026.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: North Carolina requires Election Day polling places and early-voting sites to be accessible, and every voting site must have at least one accessible voting machine that allows voters with disabilities to mark a ballot privately and independently. Eligible voters who cannot enter a voting location without physical assistance because of age or disability may use curbside voting at every Election Day polling place and early-voting site. Voters who qualify for assistance may receive help marking their ballot under state and federal rules. Blind and visually impaired voters may request, mark and return an accessible absentee ballot online through the NC Absentee Ballot Portal using a system compatible with screen readers.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible machines, curbside voting and accessible absentee voting
accessible_voting.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Help for Voters with Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: NCSBE confirms at least one accessible voting machine at every Election Day precinct and early-voting site. Curbside voting is offered at every voting site for voters unable to enter without physical assistance because of age or disability. Blind and visually impaired registered voters have a particularly significant accommodation: they may request, mark and return an accessible absentee ballot online. This is a limited accessibility system, not general online voting.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: North Carolina provides expedited registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible military members, qualifying spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living outside the United States under UOCAVA and state law. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request a ballot through the North Carolina Military/Overseas Voter Services Portal or on paper. The registration and ballot-request deadline is generally 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the day before Election Day. Covered voters may receive their ballots using authorized electronic delivery methods. North Carolina's rules for military and overseas voters differ from ordinary civilian absentee voting, so covered voters should use the dedicated State Board guidance.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA and Military/Overseas Voter Services Portal available
military_overseas.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Military and Overseas Voting
military_overseas.internal_note: NCSBE directly identifies covered military categories including active and reserve Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force and Coast Guard members, Merchant Marine, commissioned Public Health Service and NOAA corps, activated National Guard/state militia and qualifying spouses/dependents. Covered overseas citizens include certain former North Carolina residents living abroad. The FPCA deadline is generally 5:00 p.m. ET the day before Election Day. NCSBE updated its UOCAVA guidance in July 2026, so current 2026 procedures should control over older descriptions.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: North Carolina college and university students may register and vote in the county where they live while attending school if they do not intend to return to their former home after graduation. A student who does not yet know where they will live after college may register in the college community or at the former home. A student who intends to return to the former home after graduation should remain registered there. Students using same-day registration while living on campus may prove residence with qualifying documentation from their educational institution. Approved student photo ID cards from participating institutions may also be used as voter photo identification through December 31, 2026.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may register at a qualifying college or home residence
student_voting.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Registering as a College Student
student_voting.internal_note: NCSBE has unusually specific student-residency guidance. Students who do not intend to return to their former home after graduation may register in the college county; students uncertain about their post-college residence may use either the college community or former home; students intending to return should remain registered at the former home. Approved student IDs for the 2025-26 election cycle remain acceptable statewide through December 31, 2026.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Registered North Carolina voters can find their official sample ballot through the State Board of Elections Voter Search after ballots have been finalized. Enter your name, open your voter record and look for the Your Sample Ballot section. Voters may also use the NC Absentee Ballot Portal's sample-ballot option to practice making selections and download a copy. Sample ballots are not available until election officials finalize them.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Find your finalized sample ballot in Voter Search
sample_ballot.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections — Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.internal_note: NCSBE directly instructs registered voters to retrieve voter-specific sample ballots through Voter Search. The NC Absentee Ballot Portal also provides Option 4 for an accessible sample ballot. The state explicitly warns that sample ballots appear only after finalization, so the 2026 General Election ballot should be rechecked as Election Day approaches.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: North Carolina State Board of Elections, P.O. Box 27255, Raleigh, NC 27611-7255. Phone: 919-814-0700. Toll-free accessibility assistance: 866-522-4723. Fax: 919-715-0135. Email: elections.sboe@ncsbe.gov. For voter-specific registration, polling-place, absentee-ballot or local early-voting questions, contact your county board of elections.
contact.source_name: North Carolina State Board of Elections
contact.internal_note: NCSBE's current pages consistently verify P.O. Box 27255, Raleigh, NC 27611-7255; [elections.sboe@ncsbe.gov](mailto:elections.sboe@ncsbe.gov); 919-814-0700; and 919-715-0135. The disability-voting page verifies the 866-522-4723 toll-free accessibility number. The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the North Carolina State Board of Elections website for official statewide election information. The Voter Search provides registration status, Election Day polling places and finalized sample ballots. County boards of elections administer local voter registration records, early-voting sites, Election Day polling places, absentee ballots and other voter-specific election functions.
